regions.name: Connacht
regions.history: The poorest of Ireland's four provinces sent thousands of men to the Connaught Rangers, a regiment that fought in France, at Gallipoli and in Mesopotamia.

regions.name: Leinster
regions.history: Dublin's province: Irishmen joined the British Army here in large numbers, while the Easter Rising of 1916 broke out in Dublin itself.

regions.name: Munster
regions.history: Southern Ireland's province gave the Munster Fusiliers, who landed from the River Clyde at Gallipoli's V Beach in April 1915.

regions.name: West Country
regions.history: Plymouth's dockyard and the Channel ports of the West Country kept the Royal Navy and the convoys to France supplied.

regions.name: Gibraltar
regions.history: The Rock guarded the narrow mouth of the Mediterranean, a coaling and repair station for the Allied fleets and a base against U-boats.

regions.name: Ulster
regions.history: Ulster raised the 36th (Ulster) Division, which suffered terribly on the first day of the Somme, 1 July 1916.

regions.name: Wales
regions.history: Welsh coal fuelled the Royal Navy's ships; the 38th (Welsh) Division took Mametz Wood on the Somme in July 1916.

regions.name: Highlands
regions.history: Highland regiments such as the Black Watch and the Seaforths fought from Mons to the end; Scapa Flow in Orkney was the Grand Fleet's anchorage.

regions.name: Egypt
regions.history: A British protectorate from 1914, Egypt guarded the Suez Canal, beat off an Ottoman attack on it in 1915, and was the base for the campaign into Palestine.

regions.name: East Anglia
regions.history: Flat farmland facing Germany across the North Sea: its coast was raided by the German fleet and bombed by Zeppelins.

regions.name: London
regions.history: The Empire's capital and its greatest city: bombed by Zeppelins and Gotha bombers, and the heart of Britain's war industry and finance.

regions.name: Lowlands
regions.history: Glasgow's shipyards on the Clyde built warships and merchant ships by the hundred, and its factories turned out shells.

regions.name: Northern England
regions.history: Mill towns and coalfields that raised whole 'Pals' battalions; Hartlepool, Scarborough and Whitby were shelled by German warships in December 1914.

regions.name: Midlands
regions.history: England's workshop: Birmingham and the Black Country made rifles, shells and, at Lincoln nearby, the first tanks.

regions.name: Cyprus
regions.history: Annexed by Britain when the Ottoman Empire entered the war in November 1914; a quiet island on the sea road to Egypt.

regions.name: Malta
regions.history: The 'nurse of the Mediterranean': its hospitals took in tens of thousands of wounded from Gallipoli and Salonika.

regions.name: Brittany
regions.history: Brittany sent its farmers and fishermen to the trenches by the hundred thousand; its port of Brest received the American convoys from 1917.

regions.name: Casablanca
regions.history: Atlantic Morocco, a French protectorate since 1912, sent its tirailleurs and spahis to fight in France.

regions.name: Fez
regions.history: The old imperial city of Morocco, from which France ruled its new protectorate and recruited Moroccan regiments.

regions.name: Oran
regions.history: Western Algeria, French for eighty years, whose regiments of Zouaves and tirailleurs fought on the Western Front.

regions.name: Normandy
regions.history: Normandy's ports, Le Havre and Rouen, were the British Army's great supply bases in France.

regions.name: Constantine
regions.history: Eastern Algeria, a recruiting ground for the Armée d'Afrique that fought at the Marne and at Verdun.

regions.name: Aquitaine
regions.history: Bordeaux briefly became France's capital in September 1914, when the government left Paris before the Marne.

regions.name: Loire
regions.history: The Loire valley lay far behind the lines: hospitals, depots and, from 1917, American camps and supply lines.

regions.name: Artois
regions.history: The coalfields round Arras and Lens, fought over from 1914 to 1918: Vimy Ridge, taken by the Canadians in April 1917, and Loos in 1915.

regions.name: Limousin
regions.history: A quiet upland of farms in central France, and a byword for the generals 'sent to Limoges' when Joffre dismissed them.

regions.name: Burgundy
regions.history: Vineyards and farmland behind the front; Dijon was a rail junction for the armies in the east.

regions.name: Paris
regions.history: The capital, saved at the Marne in September 1914 (partly by soldiers sent out in its taxis) and shelled by the German long-range guns in 1918.

regions.name: Languedoc
regions.history: The wine country of the south, far from the fighting, which sent its men north and its wine to the trenches as the soldiers' pinard.

regions.name: Picardy
regions.history: The Somme: the great Anglo-French offensive of 1916, and the German spring offensive's push towards Amiens in 1918.

regions.name: Champagne
regions.history: The front ran through Champagne for four years: the battles of 1915, the failed Nivelle offensive of 1917, and the Marne again in 1918.

regions.name: Lyon
regions.history: France's second city became an arsenal and a centre of industry once the north was occupied.

regions.name: Verdun
regions.history: The fortress city where France and Germany fought the longest battle of the war, from February to December 1916: 'They shall not pass.'

regions.name: Tunisia
regions.history: A French protectorate whose port of Bizerte sheltered the Allied fleets and the remains of the Serbian army in 1916.

regions.name: Algiers
regions.history: The capital of French Algeria, centre of the Armée d'Afrique that crossed to France in 1914.

regions.name: Nancy
regions.history: Lorraine's French capital, saved in the Battle of the Grand Couronné in September 1914, a few miles from the German border.

regions.name: Provence
regions.history: Marseille received the troops of the Empire, from India, Indochina and Africa, and sent the armies to Salonika.

regions.name: Corsica
regions.history: The island sent a great many of its men to the war; a quiet corner of France's Mediterranean.

regions.name: Rhineland
regions.history: The Rhine's industrial west, with Cologne's fortress and bridges, through which the German armies marched to Belgium in August 1914.

regions.name: Lorraine
regions.history: German since 1871: Metz was one of the strongest fortresses in Europe, and the French attack here in August 1914 was beaten back with heavy losses.

regions.name: Lower Alsace
regions.history: Strasbourg's Alsace, German since 1871; France's war aim was to take it back.

regions.name: Hesse
regions.history: Farm country and the cities of Darmstadt and Frankfurt, deep in the German heartland.

regions.name: Upper Alsace
regions.history: Southern Alsace and Mulhouse, briefly taken by the French in August 1914; the Vosges peaks above it were fought over all war.

regions.name: Westphalia
regions.history: The Ruhr: coal, steel and Krupp's gun works at Essen, the forge of the German army.

regions.name: Schleswig
regions.history: The North Sea and Baltic coasts: Kiel and Wilhelmshaven were the High Seas Fleet's harbours, and the sailors' revolt began at Kiel in 1918.

regions.name: Baden
regions.history: The Black Forest and the upper Rhine, facing France across the river.

regions.name: Bavaria
regions.history: The southern kingdom kept its own army, whose regiments fought at Ypres, on the Somme and at Verdun.

regions.name: Hanover
regions.history: Prussian province of farms and moor; its regiments marched into Belgium in 1914.

regions.name: Wurttemberg
regions.history: A kingdom with its own army corps; its mountain troops, with a young Erwin Rommel, took Monte Matajur at Caporetto in 1917.

regions.name: Berlin
regions.history: The Kaiser's capital, where the war was declared in August 1914 and the revolution of November 1918 ended the monarchy.

regions.name: Thuringia
regions.history: Small duchies of forest and workshops in the middle of Germany.

regions.name: Franconia
regions.history: Northern Bavaria and Nuremberg, a centre of German industry.

regions.name: Saxony
regions.history: A kingdom of mills, mines and Leipzig's trade, with its own army and its own corps on the Western Front.

regions.name: Mecklenburg
regions.history: Flat farmland on the Baltic, among the quietest places in the Empire.

regions.name: Pomerania
regions.history: The Baltic coast and Stettin's harbour, a land of estates and farms.

regions.name: Silesia
regions.history: Coal and iron in the east, the third great industrial region of Germany, facing Russian Poland.

regions.name: East Prussia
regions.history: Invaded by Russia in August 1914; at Tannenberg and the Masurian Lakes the Germans destroyed two Russian armies.

regions.name: Posen
regions.history: Prussia's Polish province, whose Poles rose in revolt at the end of 1918.

regions.name: West Prussia
regions.history: Danzig and the lower Vistula; the corridor at the heart of Poland's claims after the war.

regions.name: Tyrol
regions.history: The Alpine front against Italy ran through the Tyrol's peaks and glaciers, where both armies fought in snow and blasted mines under the summits.

regions.name: Dalmatia
regions.history: The Adriatic coast and the naval harbour of Cattaro, from which Austrian U-boats and cruisers raided the Otranto barrage.

regions.name: Carniola
regions.history: Slovene lands behind the Isonzo, where Italy attacked eleven times between 1915 and 1917.

regions.name: Pilsen
regions.history: Western Bohemia, home of the Škoda works that built the Empire's heaviest siege guns, the mortars that broke the Belgian forts in 1914.

regions.name: Prague
regions.history: Bohemia's capital: its Czech soldiers fought for the Emperor, while Czech exiles worked for independence, declared here in October 1918.

regions.name: Upper Austria
regions.history: Linz and the Danube valley, in the quiet German-speaking heart of the Empire.

regions.name: Styria
regions.history: Graz and the iron of the Erzberg, which fed the Empire's arms works.

regions.name: Moravia
regions.history: Brno's textile mills and the farms of Moravia, between Bohemia and Galicia.

regions.name: Vienna
regions.history: The Habsburg capital, where the ultimatum to Serbia was written in July 1914 and the old Emperor Franz Joseph died in 1916.

regions.name: Transdanubia
regions.history: Western Hungary, a land of farms and the great lake Balaton, which fed the Empire.

regions.name: Croatia
regions.history: The Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia, whose regiments fought in Serbia and on the Isonzo.

regions.name: Krakow
regions.history: The fortress city of western Galicia, which the Russians reached in late 1914 but never took.

regions.name: Upper Hungary
regions.history: The mountains of today's Slovakia, whose Carpathian passes the Russians tried to force in the winter of 1914-15.

regions.name: Banat
regions.history: Rich farmland on the lower Danube, facing Serbia across the river.

regions.name: Budapest
regions.history: Hungary's capital, the Empire's second city and centre of its milling and industry.

regions.name: Bosnia
regions.history: Sarajevo, where Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot on 28 June 1914, the spark of the war.

regions.name: Debrecen
regions.history: The Great Hungarian Plain, a land of horses, grain and cattle.

regions.name: Lemberg
regions.history: Eastern Galicia and its capital, taken by the Russians in September 1914 and won back in the summer of 1915.

regions.name: Transylvania
regions.history: Invaded by Romania in August 1916; the Central Powers threw the Romanians back within weeks.

regions.name: Bukovina
regions.history: The Empire's far eastern corner, which changed hands several times between Austria and Russia, last in the Brusilov offensive of 1916.

regions.name: Piedmont
regions.history: Turin's industry, with FIAT's works, armed Italy's war.

regions.name: Tuscany
regions.history: Florence and the Tuscan hills, far behind the front.

regions.name: Sardinia
regions.history: The island raised the famous Sassari Brigade, which fought on the Carso and the Asiago plateau.

regions.name: Palermo
regions.history: Western Sicily, whose men were called up in their thousands for the Alpine front.

regions.name: Lombardy
regions.history: Milan's factories, the industrial heart of Italy's war effort.

regions.name: Marche
regions.history: The Adriatic coast, shelled by the Austrian fleet on the very day Italy entered the war in May 1915.

regions.name: Emilia
regions.history: Bologna and the Po valley's farms, which fed the armies on the Isonzo.

regions.name: Venetia
regions.history: Venice and the Piave: after Caporetto the Italian line held on the Piave and Monte Grappa, and won at Vittorio Veneto in 1918.

regions.name: Friuli
regions.history: The Isonzo front, where Italy fought eleven battles before the breakthrough at Caporetto in October 1917.

regions.name: Rome
regions.history: Italy's capital, where the government chose war against Austria-Hungary in May 1915.

regions.name: Abruzzo
regions.history: Mountain shepherds and farmers, whose men were drafted into the Alpine and infantry regiments.

regions.name: Rhodes
regions.history: The Dodecanese, taken by Italy from the Ottomans in 1912.

regions.name: Cyrenaica
regions.history: Eastern Libya, where the Senussi rose against the Italians and against the British in Egypt.

regions.name: Tripolitania
regions.history: Western Libya, taken from the Ottomans in 1911-12 and largely lost to rebellion during the war.

regions.name: Naples
regions.history: Italy's largest southern city and port, a gathering place for the troops of the south.

regions.name: Apulia
regions.history: The heel of Italy and the Otranto barrage, which tried to bottle up the Austrian fleet in the Adriatic.

regions.name: Catania
regions.history: Eastern Sicily and Etna's slopes, a land of farms and sulphur mines.

regions.name: Calabria
regions.history: The toe of Italy, a poor land whose men emigrated before the war and were called home to fight.

regions.name: Lodz
regions.history: The textile city of Russian Poland, around which Germans and Russians fought in November and December 1914.

regions.name: West Finland
regions.history: The Grand Duchy's western coast, whose young men went secretly to Germany to train as Jäger.

regions.name: Bessarabia
regions.history: Between the Prut and the Dniester, joined to Romania in 1918.

regions.name: Lublin
regions.history: Southern Russian Poland, fought over in the first battles of 1914 and lost to the Central Powers in 1915.

regions.name: Courland
regions.history: The Baltic coast, occupied by Germany in 1915 and held to the end of the war.

regions.name: Warsaw
regions.history: The capital of Russian Poland, given up to the Germans in August 1915.

regions.name: Grodno
regions.history: A fortress city on the Neman, given up in the great retreat of 1915.

regions.name: Estonia
regions.history: The northern Baltic lands, occupied by Germany early in 1918.

regions.name: Kovno
regions.history: The Kaunas fortress, which fell to the Germans in August 1915 after a short siege.

regions.name: Podolia
regions.history: The Ukrainian borderland behind Brusilov's armies in 1916.

regions.name: Volhynia
regions.history: Lutsk and the Volhynian fortresses, where Brusilov's offensive of June 1916 broke the Austrian line.

regions.name: Vilna
regions.history: Lithuania's capital, occupied by Germany in September 1915.

regions.name: Riga
regions.history: The Baltic port that fell to the Germans in September 1917 after a new kind of short bombardment.

regions.name: East Finland
regions.history: Karelia's forests and lakes on the border with Russia proper.

regions.name: Helsingfors
regions.history: Finland's capital, which declared independence in December 1917.

regions.name: Pskov
regions.history: Where Tsar Nicholas II abdicated aboard his train in March 1917.

regions.name: Minsk
regions.history: The headquarters of Russia's Western Front, behind the lines that stood still from 1915 to 1917.

regions.name: Petrograd
regions.history: The capital renamed in 1914, where the revolutions of February and October 1917 took Russia out of the war.

regions.name: Vitebsk
regions.history: White Russian lands behind the front of 1915-17.

regions.name: Kiev
regions.history: The Ukrainian capital, which declared a republic in 1917 and came under German occupation in 1918.

regions.name: Moscow
regions.history: Russia's old capital and largest city, centre of its industry and, from 1918, the Bolsheviks' capital.

regions.name: Crimea
regions.history: Sevastopol and the Black Sea Fleet, which German and Ottoman warships shelled in October 1914.

regions.name: Smolensk
regions.history: The old road to Moscow, deep behind the front.

regions.name: Chernigov
regions.history: Farmland north of Kiev, deep behind the front.

regions.name: Odessa
regions.history: Russia's great Black Sea port, shelled by Ottoman ships in October 1914, which brought the Ottomans into the war.

regions.name: Kars
regions.history: The Caucasus fortress, near which the Russians destroyed an Ottoman army at Sarıkamış in the winter of 1914-15.

regions.name: Poltava
regions.history: The wheat fields of central Ukraine.

regions.name: Kherson
regions.history: The Black Sea steppe and Nikolayev's shipyards, which built dreadnoughts for the Black Sea Fleet.

regions.name: Kharkov
regions.history: A great railway and industrial city of eastern Ukraine.

regions.name: Ekaterinoslav
regions.history: The Donbass coal and the Dnieper steel works, Russia's south.

regions.name: Rostov
regions.history: The gateway to the Caucasus on the Don.

regions.name: Kuban
regions.history: The Cossack lands of the Kuban, whose horsemen rode on every Russian front.

regions.name: Stavropol
regions.history: The steppe north of the Caucasus, a land of wheat and horses.

regions.name: Tiflis
regions.history: Georgia's capital, headquarters of Russia's Caucasus army against the Ottomans.

regions.name: Erivan
regions.history: Armenian lands on the Ottoman border, which took in refugees from the deportations of 1915.

regions.name: Adrianople
regions.history: Edirne, the old Ottoman capital in Europe, retaken from Bulgaria in 1913 and guarding the land road to Constantinople.

regions.name: Constantinople
regions.history: The Sultan's capital on the Bosporus, which the Allies tried and failed to reach through the Dardanelles in 1915.

regions.name: Smyrna
regions.history: The great Aegean port of Anatolia, rich in figs, tobacco and trade.

regions.name: Palestine
regions.history: Gaza, Beersheba and Jerusalem: the British broke through here in late 1917 and entered Jerusalem in December.

regions.name: Trebizond
regions.history: The Black Sea port taken by the Russians in April 1916.

regions.name: Bursa
regions.history: The first Ottoman capital, a city of silk below Mount Uludağ.

regions.name: Angora
regions.history: Ankara, a small town of central Anatolia on the Berlin to Baghdad railway's route.

regions.name: Konya
regions.history: The heart of the Anatolian plateau, a junction of the Baghdad railway.

regions.name: Adana
regions.history: The cotton plain of Cilicia, where the Baghdad railway had to cross the Taurus mountains.

regions.name: Sivas
regions.history: Central Anatolia, behind the Caucasus front.

regions.name: Aleppo
regions.history: A great Syrian market city on the Baghdad railway, taken by the Arabs and the British in October 1918.

regions.name: Lebanon
regions.history: Mount Lebanon and Beirut, struck by a terrible famine during the war.

regions.name: Baghdad
regions.history: The prize of the Mesopotamian campaign, taken by the British in March 1917 after their defeat at Kut the year before.

regions.name: Damascus
regions.history: The Syrian capital, entered by the Arab revolt and the British in October 1918.

regions.name: Diarbekir
regions.history: The upper Tigris, a province of Kurds and Armenians in the east.

regions.name: Erzerum
regions.history: The fortress of eastern Anatolia, stormed by the Russians in the snow in February 1916.

regions.name: Mosul
regions.history: Northern Mesopotamia on the Tigris, still in Ottoman hands at the armistice of October 1918.

regions.name: Vidin
regions.history: The Danube fortress in Bulgaria's north-west corner, facing Serbia and Romania.

regions.name: Kyustendil
regions.history: Western Bulgaria, from which the Bulgarian army struck into Serbian Macedonia in October 1915.

regions.name: Gumuljina
regions.history: Western Thrace and Bulgaria's outlet to the Aegean, won in the Balkan Wars.

regions.name: Sofia
regions.history: Bulgaria's capital, which joined the Central Powers in October 1915 and asked for an armistice in September 1918.

regions.name: Tarnovo
regions.history: The old capital of medieval Bulgaria, in the hills of the north.

regions.name: Plovdiv
regions.history: The Thracian plain, a land of wheat, tobacco and roses.

regions.name: Burgas
regions.history: Bulgaria's southern Black Sea port.

regions.name: Varna
regions.history: Bulgaria's main Black Sea port, a base for German U-boats in the war.

regions.name: Flanders
regions.history: Ypres and the Yser: the last corner of Belgium left free, held by Belgian and British soldiers through four years of mud.

regions.name: South Albania
regions.history: Southern Albania, occupied in turn by Greece, Italy and France during the war.

regions.name: Wallonia
regions.history: Liège and its forts, the first fortress the German army had to break in August 1914; the rest of Wallonia lived under occupation.

regions.name: Oltenia
regions.history: Romania west of the Olt, overrun by the Central Powers in late 1916.

regions.name: Moldavia
regions.history: Iași and the Romanian north-east, where Romania's army held on after Bucharest fell, winning at Mărășești in 1917.

regions.name: Montenegro
regions.history: The small mountain kingdom that fought beside Serbia and was overrun in January 1916.

regions.name: Belgrade
regions.history: Serbia's capital on the Danube, shelled from across the river on the war's first night and taken in October 1915.

regions.name: Macedonia
regions.history: The Salonika front, where the Allies faced the Bulgarians from 1915 and broke through at Dobro Pole in September 1918.

regions.name: North Albania
regions.history: Scutari and the mountains of a new, fragile state, crossed by the Serbian army's winter retreat to the sea in 1915.

regions.name: Peloponnese
regions.history: Southern Greece, a land of olives and currants far from the fighting.

regions.name: Nis
regions.history: Serbia's wartime capital in 1914-15, before the great retreat over the mountains.

regions.name: Epirus
regions.history: The Greek north-west, on the border with Albania.

regions.name: Thessaly
regions.history: The plain of central Greece, its granary.

regions.name: Bucharest
regions.history: Romania's capital, which joined the Allies in August 1916 and was taken by the Central Powers in December.

regions.name: Athens
regions.history: The Greek capital, divided between a king who wanted to stay neutral and a prime minister, Venizelos, who brought Greece into the war in 1917.

regions.name: Crete
regions.history: The island joined to Greece in 1913, the homeland of Venizelos.

regions.name: Dobruja
regions.history: The Black Sea coast between the Danube and the sea, taken from Romania by the Bulgarians and Germans in 1916.
